summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (feasibility decision), and Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped. The deterministic gate set simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false. The input gate failed because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction returned an empty floorplan and no power. The scientific gate also failed. The paper (Thermal Simulation of a CPU Based on Model Order Reduction, W4206159291) is a transient 3 ms FEniCS DNS of a 3D layered Alpha EV6 chip (129x129x7 mesh) used to train a POD reduced-order model. It compares 1-, 3- and 5-mode POD against the DNS at the functional unit C hot spot and on x/y profiles at t=3 ms. The extracted experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace and cannot represent the pulsed, time-resolved observable. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration. No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison with the paper is made. The paper's temperature values appear only in figures, were not digitized, and are null in the extraction. Even a hypothetical run would not match on location, aggregation (time-resolved point versus steady), regime, or boundary assumptions (adiabatic sides and top, Robin substrate bottom with an unreported coefficient). No claim of replication or agreement is supported, and only qualitative sensitivity discussion is warranted: a 2D steady model could at most indicate relative hot-spot tendencies, not the paper's dynamic results.
limitations: Studio was not run (status skipped); there is no simulated result to assess.
Gate verdict is not_2d_applicable with simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false; no replication is claimed.
Input validation failed: no blocks and no power_w object were supplied for the custom experiment.
The original is a 3D layered chip (7 mesh layers) with a device layer and substrate; a 2D model cannot capture vertical conduction or the substrate Robin cooling path.

The original is a transient 3 ms simulation with pulsed power (3.333 us period, 10k-cycle average at 3 GHz); a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and cannot reproduce the unit C dynamic temperature.
The solver differs: FEniCS FEM DNS plus POD-Galerkin ROM with 1/3/5 modes cannot be reproduced by a Studio solver.
The boundary conditions are adiabatic sides and top with a Robin substrate bottom at 0 C ambient and an unreported coefficient; no package, heat sink or realistic cooling stack is modeled.
Numeric block geometry for the Alpha EV6 floorplan is not published (Fig. 1 is graphical only), and per-block powers for units A, B and C are not given.
Chip dimensions, layer thicknesses and material properties (k, density, specific heat) are missing.
The paper's observable (hot-spot temperature rise above ambient) exists only in plots and was not digitized; no numeric value is available for comparison.
Linked assets (microprocessor trend data, FEniCS, HotSpot) are not pinned packet assets and do not demonstrate the availability of the thermal inputs; no code or data availability statement exists.
Evidence items lack valid page or asset locators per the gate, and adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved.
